feature: Picking a value to animate answers faster
summary: Choosing a value from Animate a property used to freeze the app for about 200 ms on every pick. It now holds about 80 ms: the list closes first and the value arrives a frame later, and the panel no longer builds and throws away 180 hidden dropdowns each time.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a recording, press T, click the canvas and type a title, then press Command-Return.
In the panel's Properties section, click Animate a property.
Click Position in the list, and watch the list close, the Position row arrive armed and its lane open on the timeline.
Open the list again and pick Scale, then Blur, one after the other at your normal speed.
Press Command-Z after a pick and watch the row and its lane go.

evaluate: Does a pick now feel like it answers at once, or can you still feel a catch?
Does the list closing a frame before the row appears ever read as a flicker?
Is opening the list (still about 110 ms) the slower of the two to your hand?
rough: Measured on the loop's probe build, three runs each: Position 71 to 83 ms (was 186 to 237), Scale 79 to 81 ms (was 192), Blur 82 to 86 ms (was 211), Shadow 1 distance 61 ms (was 199 to 210). Not yet under the 50 ms the video success list asks for; the rest is the whole panel laying itself out again whenever focus moves or the document changes, carried by animate-a-property-opens-closes-and-keys-a-value.
Opening the list still holds about 110 ms; that task covers it too.

The probe carries walk-only markers and pays for accessibility the harness reads, together roughly a third of these numbers, so the shipping app should feel quicker than the figures above; nothing here measured the shipping build.
No mock covers how fast a pick is; the list, rows and lanes look exactly as before.
